mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE is below 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive quarters, combined with a simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST), signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity and capacity utilization, which typically precedes positive equity returns as firms expand profits over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops below 2% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is contradictory and signals a data anomaly or major sectoral reallocation; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days are expected to be highly volatile and, on average, negative due to uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises while PAYEMS also rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative or are positive when UNRATE and PAYEMS move in opposite directions in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth deceleration (GDPC1) from above 2% to below 1% over two consecutive quarters, with no offsetting rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals weakening demand without cost-push inflation, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls from >2% to <1% YoY over two quarters AND CPIAUCSL does not rise YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDP growth decelerates as described and inflation does not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for six consecutive months, regardless of GDP or labor conditions, signals robust supply-side expansion that typically boosts earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises above 0.5% per month for six consecutive months.
